messages.subject: Concurvity in DSM
parts:
Hello Distance Group,

I had a question regarding testing concurvity for a DSM in R. When I get the output matrices for between-terms concurvity, each matrix is not generally a mirror image of itself as you would expect with an normal correlation matrix. For example I have the following output:

$estimate
para s(x,y) s(PDBRUSH) s(MPAOPEN)
para 1.000000e+00 3.238864e-26 4.599797e-22 2.736765e-28
s(x,y) 1.820222e-24 1.000000e+00 8.011582e-02 2.424521e-01
s(PDBRUSH) 1.297044e-19 1.789573e-02 1.000000e+00 3.189349e-01
s(MPAOPEN) 1.230777e-25 4.408106e-02 4.217571e-01 1.000000e+00

The between terms concurvity measures should ideally be the same between redundant terms, but they are not. Is there something I am missing, or is the concurvity matrix different in some way? Any clarification would help.

While on the topic, I also was curious as to which concurvity measure (i.e., worst, observed, or estimate) is the appropriate one to use, and what is a standard cutoff range for removing highly concurve terms from the model?

Thanks,

John

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Concurvity in DSM
parts:
Hi John, hi listfolk,

To my knowledge, there is no "cutoff" for concurvity that can be
generally applied, mainly because this is still a somewhat experimental
technique in the very early stages of development. For the same reason,
I don't have too much guidance to offer on which of the measures would
be most appropriate. My usual approach is to look at the results for the
three metrics (probably paying more attention to the "estimate" type),
look at the measures then check to see if those terms with higher values
change model results when they are removed. Assessing that kind of model
structure instability seems like the most useful application of concurvity.

As for the asymmetry of the resulting matrix, I think this is okay since
the measure displayed is related to the values of the norm of one smooth
divided by the norm of another (max of the norms or whatever). symmetric
entries are reciprocals of each other (e.g., f/g or g/f) but I don't
think there's any reason to think that these should be identical. That
being said, they probably should be about the same order I would think.

The ?concurvity manual page also has some more (albeit technical) detail.

Hope this helps!

cheers,
--dave
